rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -E '\bhonest\b|\bdelve\b|\blandscape\b|\bimportantly\b|\bcrucial\b|\bsynergize\b|\bparadigm shift\b|\bleverage\b' in body returns 0 matches

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -E '\britual\b|\bceremony\b' in body returns 0 matches for hard-banned forms

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body region (lines 1-53) carries no session biography, no TODO closure markers, no transition verbs. Tense test: all clauses state present-tense fact or future student action. Clean.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 quintet voice (Boris + Martin + Godin + Sutherland + Siilasmaa) applied. Body reads factual/direct (Boris), avoids consultancy register, peer-warm. Register clean.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to article drafts only; this is an exercise file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No named techniques paraphrased. Git worktree mechanics are tool operations, not credited techniques.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses second person consistently (6 instances of 'you'). Zero 'the student' in body. Teacher framing correctly withheld from body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms in body (worktree, session, branch, git history) earned by operation or common vocabulary. No maintainer-only jargon smuggled in.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance-shaped sentences found (no 'fine way to', 'no penalty', 'it's OK if', 'not a downgrade'). Delegation prose stands clean.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule fires on reference artifacts only; this is an exercise file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner attribution in body. Boris Cherny credit sits below maintainer cut and doesn't count.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No punchy reframes in body. Prose is instructional/mechanical, not aspirational framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body carries no vendor-defense framing or positioning vocabulary. Prose is mechanical and tool-agnostic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: M3 opener. Jargon (session, branch, worktree) earned at M1/M2 or earned inline by operational context. No premature planting.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No dangling pronouns (the one, it, that) or bypass-the-agent closers. Section closes on concrete action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The **What happened:** block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: line 53: 'You forked a sibling worktree for the quality side, opened two Claude Code sessions (one in your repo, one in the sibling), and confirmed each reads the same codebase from a different working directory. Security picks up in the main window at the next exercise. The quality side waits.' Violates three-move shape: (1) narrates student actions instead of artifact-as-subject; (2) no qualifier on what makes artifact yours; (3) includes forward-facing navigation not artifact destination. Should follow: count+noun, one qualifier, destination.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rewrite What happened block to follow three-move shape or cut it entirely since exercise produces no durable artifact

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Verbs describing student→agent use peer-flat register: ask, fork, confirm, copy. No combative verbs present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers (Fork the side worktree, Read back the worktree path, Open the quality lane, Set the two windows side by side) describe actual mechanism. No spatial metaphors contradicting reality.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negations, deictic drumroll, bold-label echo, or citation duplication. Prose is direct and mechanical.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No counted numerals stated adjacent to lists already holding structure. No redundant counts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No slogans with superlatives (only/always/never/nothing else). Prose is instructional, not aspirational.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule governs multi-file claim tracking with backing stamps. Single-file exercise has no cross-file claims.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule governs multi-file sweep procedures. Single-file judge does not reconstruct rule set mid-session.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body names what student becomes (multi-session practitioner) without naming deficiency. No corrective-gap framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Worktree earned: 'A sibling worktree is a second working directory on the same git history.' Session, branch, git history are common vocabulary. No unearned terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 file (software-engineer IC audience), not Agents 101 business-audience default.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body correctly uses 'rules' (persistent artifact) and 'session' (ambient runtime). Distinction maintained.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body carries golden path only. No troubleshooting or recovery branches in body; time-critical rescue window not applicable here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt asks Claude to fork + copy files with no structure specification beyond destination + report.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No Debrief compound moves in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: M3 voice (mechanical, multi-window framing) applied. No adjacent module's voice patterns smuggled.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No manual diffing or spot-check asked. Prompts delegate work to Claude.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a self-study simulation file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
rules_evaluated.evidence: No callout boxes present. No research-says framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Moves (fork, rename, confirm) all run in Claude Code. No editor/terminal primitives forced outside conversation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body correctly names './CLAUDE.local.md' (personal, gitignored) with layer clarity.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep '—' in body region returns 0 matches. No em-dashes in student-facing prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers use command verbs: Fork, Read back, Open, Set. All action-oriented.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Link '[Multi-session and Git survival guide]' uses title, not filename.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body names 'session' contextually as 'new Claude Code session'. Collision disambiguated.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses 'Claude' for UI invocation ('Ask Claude to fork'). No conflation with agent/LLM.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body correctly splits 'session' (Claude Code sitting) vs 'side-quest' (task). No conflation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No time-of-day phrasing (tomorrow, overnight, tonight). Module names and session-relative phrasing used.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts don't re-ask decisions. First asks Claude to fork; second asks Claude to confirm. No meta-loops.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise produces no student-authored file artifacts. Prompt destinations are system state, not files.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body prose advances student toward two-window setup. No implementation details before point-of-use. NVA-clean.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'read it', 'look at it' narration after prompt output. Prompts produce state; body moves to next action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: line 51: 'Module 3's exercises name which window the work runs in, and where the switch points are.' Subject is curriculum (Module 3's exercises), not student.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast with student as grammatical subject: 'you'll find which window the work runs in named at each exercise' or 'each exercise names which window the work runs in for you'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Session widgets appear at point of use. Moment-of-use principle honored.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses training vocabulary: session, branch, rules (memory). No invented synonyms for house terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body says 'Ask Claude to fork' (prompt noun), not 'typing fork' or 'tell it to fork'. Artifact noun register honored.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body doesn't walk through git/shell step-by-step. Asks Claude to fork; names outcome. Outcome-focused.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body avoids arc-positioning narration. Subject is student's work (opening windows, forking), not curriculum shape.
